items.title: Vanderbilt University hit in BYOD ransomware attack, data theft claimed
items.description: Vanderbilt University warns it is responding to a cyberattack claimed by the BYOD ransomware gang, which claims to have encrypted the university's databases and stolen sensitive student, employee, and research data. [...]

items.title: SEGA newsletter data breach exposes 2.2 million email addresses
items.description: Japanese gaming giant SEGA has disclosed that a data breach at its third-party newsletter provider, ARARA, exposed the email addresses of 2.2 million newsletter subscribers. [...]

items.title: CISA Announces Enhanced Reporting Form for Cyber Incidents
items.description: New questionnaire captures critical data and information that improves the agency’s ability to assess incidents, identify trends and prioritize response actions.

items.title: N-able takes cloud platform offline after 30+ "zero-days" published
items.description: N-able has taken its hosted N-central environments offline and urged on-premises customers to shut down their servers after a security researcher publicly disclosed more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities, including exploits that could let attackers take over vulnerable systems. items.title: York University breach exposed personal information dating to 2007
items.description: York University has announced it suffered a cybersecurity incident in which a threat actor stole personal information people submitted through online forms. [...]

items.title: Microsoft Fixes RCE Bug in Windows Paint After Weeks of Confusion
items.description: Last month, Microsoft disclosed a vulnerability in Microsoft Paint, but messaging regarding a patch was unclear.

items.title: Black Hat India 2026 Makes a Landmark Debut in Bengaluru, Bringing the Global Cybersecurity Community to India
items.description: Inaugural edition by Informa Markets in India brings together leading researchers, security practitioners and industry decision makers for four days of cutting-edge research, technical exchange and strategic dialogue.

items.title: France blames Iranian hackers for supermarket attacks that sparked fires
items.description: France has linked October cyberattacks that disrupted refrigeration systems at more than 700 supermarkets and other retail locations to Iranian state-backed hackers, saying the attacks caused food losses and sparked at least 15 fires. [...]

items.title: Attackers Crash Claude's 'Office Party' Flaw to Run Malicious Code on Linux
items.description: Attackers can exploit a flaw in Claude's document-processing tool by creating a temporary file that Anthropic's AI assistant can access and run on a user's machine.

items.title: New Abe Office Malware Bypasses Chrome App-Bound Encryption to Steal Browser Passwords and Cookies
items.description: A new remote-access trojan called Abe Office can steal browser passwords and cookies, even from Chrome’s App-Bound Encryption. It poses as an office helper tool and carries a valid code-signing certificate. Researchers at Rogue Authority broke its weak protections and watched the operator at work in a sandbox. items.title: Hackers Exploit Qubole's Trusted AWS Access to Breach Customer Accounts and Steal Data
items.description: An attacker broke into AWS accounts belonging to multiple Qubole customers between October 14 and October 26 and stole stored secrets and data, cloud security company Wiz said today. The attacker used credentials for an AWS account that Qubole's platform uses to reach those customers. How the attacker got those credentials has not been disclosed. items.title: Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop to Deliver Wallet-Stealing Malware
items.description: Attackers used the Ethersphere project's own release automation to publish malicious versions of two of its tools for the Swarm decentralized storage network: bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2.
